meta.subtitle: Cloud and Search drive a stronger operating line, while gain-inflated earnings and outside funding of the AI build-out make this a narrow BUY

analystSentiment.commentary: Alphabet's operating line accelerated in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, and the question for the shares is what that operating business is worth once a very large non-operating gain is set aside. Google Cloud is growing far faster than the rest of the company and earning more, advertising is still growing double digits, and operating margin widened; the financials and growth sections carry the figures. Reported earnings overstate the business: over the six months to June 30, other income, driven in the second quarter primarily by net unrealized gains on equity securities, contributed more pre-tax income than operations did. That makes the trailing P/E and the vendor's forward multiple look cheaper than the operating business is, so we value the shares on FY27E consensus earnings instead. The funding picture has also changed. Alphabet raised new equity and debt in the second quarter to pay for AI infrastructure, and free cash flow has grown little while operating cash flow climbed; the balance-sheet and cash-flow sections size both. We rate GOOGL BUY, and it is a narrow BUY: it rests on the market paying a full multiple for FY27 earnings a year from now, and the valuation section shows how small a change in that multiple, in the Bear weight or in the price turns it into a HOLD. The Street is more positive than we are, and our fair value sits below its consensus target.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Alphabet, incorporated in 1998 and headquartered in Mountain View, California, reports Google in two segments, Google Services and Google Cloud, and groups its non-Google businesses as Other Bets. Google Services covers advertising on Google Search & other properties, YouTube and Google Network properties, plus subscriptions, platforms and devices such as YouTube TV, YouTube Music and Premium, Google One, Google Play and the Pixel family of devices. Google Cloud sells consumption-based infrastructure and platform services, including the Vertex AI platform and Gemini Enterprise, along with Google Workspace, cybersecurity, data and analytics, and product sales that are primarily TPU systems. Other Bets generates revenue primarily from autonomous transportation services and internet services. Alphabet also centralizes AI research and frontier-model development at the corporate level and reports that cost as Alphabet-level activities rather than inside any segment. The vendor data behind this report carry a single consolidated line, so segment figures come from the company's July 22, 2026 earnings release. FY25 revenue was $402.8 billion, up {+ 15.1% +}. In its 10-K filed February 5, 2026, Alphabet said it generated more than 70% of total revenues from online advertising in 2025, so the durability of advertising is the assumption any Alphabet thesis rests on. The shares carry a market value of about $4.29 trillion.

thesis.label: BUY
thesis.body: Alphabet is executing well on the operating line, and the case for the shares turns on whether that execution earns a full multiple on earnings stripped of this year's investment gains. In favor: Google Cloud is growing far faster than the rest of the business and its segment profit is rising with it, advertising is still growing double digits through the AI shift, and the company has begun selling TPU systems with most of that revenue expected in 2027. Against: the earnings that make the stock look cheap rest on non-operating gains, the AI build-out is now partly funded with new equity and debt, free cash flow has not kept pace with operating cash flow, and the company itself warns that AI is reshaping advertising with no assurance it adapts. Our Base case has consensus FY27 earnings arriving and the market paying a full multiple for them a year out. On that Base, with the Bull and Bear weighted equally, the probability-weighted value clears the BUY line by a thin margin, and we say so rather than round it up into conviction.

catalysts: TPU system sales, which Alphabet began recognizing in the second quarter of 2026 and expects mostly in 2027; the growth section sets out the timing.
Further Google Cloud growth and segment profit, which the growth and moat sections size.
Evidence that AI features add to Search use rather than replace it, tracked in the growth section through Google Search & other revenue.
Continued operating margin gains as cost of revenues grows more slowly than sales, as the financials section explains.
risks: AI reshaping advertising: the company's own 10-K says there is no assurance it adapts, as the risks section details.
Funding the AI build-out with new equity, a mandatory convertible preferred and debt, which the balance-sheet and capital-allocation discussions cover.
Regulatory action on Google's distribution arrangements after the EC decision upheld in July 2026, covered in the risks section.
A narrow call: a lower Base multiple, a heavier Bear weight or a slightly higher price turns BUY into HOLD, as the valuation section shows.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary:
Revenue grew from $257.6 billion in FY21 to $402.8 billion in FY25, and growth picked up from +8.7% in FY23 to +13.9% in FY24 and +15.1% in FY25. Operating margin rose from 26.5% in FY22 to 32.1% in FY24 and held at 32.0% in FY25, while gross margin widened to 59.7%. The quarter ended June 30, 2026 pushed further. Revenue rose {+ 24% +} year over year to $119.8 billion, {+ 23% +} in constant currency, which the company called its 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth. Operating income rose {+ 30% +} to $40,770 million and operating margin widened by 2 percentage points to 34%. The margin gain came from cost of revenues, which rose 18%, primarily on depreciation, TAC, inventory and other costs, content acquisition and infrastructure operations. Operating expenses rose 27%, faster than revenue, led by employee compensation, advertising and promotion, and depreciation. Depreciation, primarily on technical infrastructure, sits in both lists; that is where the capital spending in the cash-flow section reaches the income statement.

Below the operating line the quarter is not representative. Other income (expense), net was a $98.0 billion net gain, against $2,662 million a year earlier, which the company attributes primarily to net unrealized gains on equity securities. That lifted net income available to common stockholders {+ 298% +} to $112,107 million and diluted EPS {+ 294% +} to $9.11. Over the six months to June 30, 2026, other income of $135,699 million exceeded operating income of $80,466 million, and diluted EPS reached $14.24. FY25 shows the same effect on a smaller scale: net income of $132.2 billion was above operating income of $129.0 billion. Unrealized gains need not recur and can turn into losses, so GAAP EPS and the 54.8% trailing net margin overstate what the operations earn. We read the business through operating income.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary: Alphabet closed FY25 with $126.8 billion of cash and short-term investments against total debt of $48.5 billion and equity of $415.3 billion. The vendor's net debt of $17.8 billion matches total debt less cash and cash equivalents of $30,708 million at December 31, 2025, so it leaves out marketable securities; counting them, liquid assets were well above debt. The first half of 2026 enlarged the balance sheet. By June 30, 2026, total cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities had reached $242,474 million, long-term debt $98,165 million against $46,547 million at year-end, property and equipment, net $321,212 million against $246,597 million, and total stockholders' equity $640,480 million. Part of that came from outside capital. In June 2026 the company issued Class A and Class C stock and 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred stock for aggregate net proceeds of $49.6 billion, to be used for general corporate purposes including capital expenditures to scale AI infrastructure and global compute, and in the second quarter it issued senior unsecured notes for net proceeds of $20.3 billion. It also entered into an ATM program to sell up to $40.0 billion of Class A and Class C stock, with proceeds primarily intended to meet tax obligations associated with employee equity grants; no shares had been sold under it by June 30. Class A, Class B and Class C shares outstanding rose to 12,230 million from 12,088 million over the six months. Solvency is not the question: debt is small against equity, the trailing current ratio is 2.72 and trailing interest coverage is 65.6x. The question is per share, because the build-out is now partly paid for with new shares and with preferred stock that is mandatory convertible.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary: Operating cash flow rose from $91.7 billion in FY21 to $164.7 billion in FY25, but capital expenditure kept pace with it at the end of that run. Capex rose from $52.5 billion in FY24 to {- $91.4 billion -} in FY25 and absorbed nearly all of that year's increase in operating cash flow. Free cash flow therefore moved only from $67.0 billion in FY21 to $73.3 billion in FY25, with a low of $60.0 billion in FY22, and the free-cash-flow margin fell from 26.0% to 18.2%. The company ties the spending to AI: its 10-K names AI-optimized infrastructure, including its custom TPUs, among its investments, and the June 2026 equity raise was earmarked in part for capital expenditures to scale AI infrastructure. The first-half growth in property and equipment (balance-sheet section) shows the spending still rising in 2026. Cash returned to shareholders moved the other way in FY25: share repurchases fell to $45.7 billion from $62.2 billion in FY24, the lowest of the five years shown, while dividends paid rose to $10.0 billion from $7.4 billion in FY24, when the table first shows a dividend. The dividend yield is 0.25%. The cash engine still funds both investment and returns, but the share of operating cash flow left after capex has been shrinking, and that is the mechanism behind our Bear case.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: At $351.16 on September 22, 2026, the shares trade at 17.6x trailing earnings and 17.0x on the vendor's next-twelve-months measure, which lines up with FY26E consensus EPS of $20.62. Neither is a clean read of the operating business. Both rest on earnings lifted by the investment gains booked through June 30 that the financials section describes, so the operations are more expensive than those multiples suggest. The page offers one forward multiple without those gains: 23.6x FY27E consensus EPS of $14.91, a year that does not include the 2026 gains already booked. For a value set a year out on FY27E, the like-for-like reference is today's current-year multiple. The page's current-year figure is the vendor multiple above, which sits on gain-inflated FY26E EPS, and the page shows no clean version of it. We therefore cannot tell whether the multiple our Base assumes is a held multiple or a re-rating, and the scenario commentary treats it as the assumption that decides the label. On other measures, trailing EV/EBITDA is 23.3x, trailing price to sales is 9.6x, and the trailing free-cash-flow yield is 1.2%, a thin cash return at this price. No peer multiples are on the page, so we draw no relative comparison. The shares trade below a 52-week high of $408.61 and above a low of $235.84; no captured headline explains the move from the high. The Street is more positive than we are: 56 of 61 analysts rate the shares Buy, 5 Hold and none Sell, and the consensus target is $429.46, 22.3% above the price, with a median of $430.00 and a range of $340.00 to $515.00.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Google Cloud keeps compounding as the TPU system revenue the company expects mostly in 2027 arrives, Google Search & other keeps growing double digits as AI features add to query growth, and FY27 estimates rise. Anchor: the shares reach $515.00, the top of the Street's target range, a level that needs higher FY27 estimates, a richer multiple than today's 23.6x on FY27E, or both.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Consensus FY27E EPS of $14.91 is delivered, advertising grows near its current pace and capital spending stays high. Anchor: 28x FY27E EPS, which is what today's 23.6x one-year-forward multiple becomes a year from now if earnings then grow by about a fifth, slower than the FY27E revenue growth consensus expects. The value sits just below the $429.46 consensus target.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: AI changes how people search and squeezes Search monetization, regulators press further on distribution after the EC decision, and capital spending keeps outrunning free cash flow, so FY27 estimates fall and the market stops paying up for them. Anchor: 17.0x FY27E consensus EPS, today's current-year multiple. That means paying for FY27 earnings, which carry none of the 2026 gains, what the market now pays for gain-inflated FY26E earnings; the multiple stands in for estimate cuts as well as the de-rating.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Weighting the Base at 60% and the Bull and Bear at 20% each gives a fair value of $404.18, expected upside of +15.1% and bear-case downside of 27.8%, a reward/risk of 0.54×. That clears the BUY thresholds of +10.0% and 0.50×, but narrowly, and three inputs decide it.

The first is the Base multiple. 28x assumes the market keeps today's one-year-forward rating a year from now. In favor: operating margin widened in the second quarter, Cloud profit is rising and Google Search & other is still growing double digits. Against: the page shows no clean current-year multiple to test it against, depreciation is rising with the build-out, and the shares have already come down from their 52-week high. A Base one turn lower, at 27x, derives HOLD.

The second is the Bear weight. We give the Bear that weight because the current operating data run against its story: Search is growing, not shrinking, and margins are widening. The case for a heavier Bear is the outside funding, the thin free-cash-flow yield and the company's own warning on AI and advertising. Five more points on the Bear, taken from either the Base or the Bull, derives HOLD. We judge the lighter weight the better one, and the call is close.

The third is the price. On these scenarios a close only a few dollars above the report-day price derives HOLD, so the BUY holds only near that price. In the other direction, moving five points from the Bear to the Bull keeps BUY and does not reach STRONG BUY, which needs +20.0% and 1.00×.

The Bear price sits above the 52-week low, a level the shares traded below within the year, so it is a real downside rather than a remote one. The $360–$470 target range brackets the Base and leaves out both tails. Our fair value is below the Street's consensus target because our Base assumes the market holds, rather than raises, the forward multiple it pays today.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The vendor data carry one consolidated line; the July 22, 2026 earnings release gives segment operating income for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Google Services earned $39,544 million, against $33,063 million a year earlier, and remains the profit engine. Google Cloud earned $8,814 million against $2,826 million, so it was already profitable a year ago and is now a material second profit pool. Other Bets lost $1,799 million, a wider loss than the $1,246 million a year earlier. Alphabet-level activities, which primarily reflect expenses for shared AI research and development, cost $5,789 million against $3,372 million. Segment profits are stated before those central costs and the Other Bets loss, so they add up to more than consolidated operating income. The rising central cost pays for the frontier models that, in the company's words, serve all of its businesses.

moatFactors.name: Search and advertising reach
moatFactors.body: Google advertising brought in $81,629 million of the quarter's revenue, and Google Search & other accounts for most of it. The advantage rests on reach: Alphabet pays TAC to browser providers, mobile carriers, original equipment manufacturers and software developers that make its search access points available, and to Google Network partners for ads on their properties. That reach across devices is what advertisers pay for. It is also the pool the 10-K's AI warning is aimed at, as the risks section sets out.

moatFactors.name: YouTube
moatFactors.body: YouTube earns from advertising and from subscriptions such as YouTube TV, YouTube Music and Premium and NFL Sunday Ticket, so it does not depend on a single revenue stream. In the July 22, 2026 release, Sundar Pichai said over 1.7 billion unique viewers watched World Cup-related videos during the FIFA World Cup 2026, a measure of reach rather than revenue. The offset is cost: YouTube licenses content and pays providers based on revenues generated, subscriber counts or a flat fee, so content acquisition costs rise with the business.

moatFactors.name: Cloud infrastructure and AI models
moatFactors.body: Google Cloud pairs AI infrastructure, including Alphabet's custom TPUs, with the Vertex AI platform and Gemini models, and Alphabet funds frontier-model research centrally for all its businesses. In the same release Pichai said nearly 90% of the Fortune 100 use Gemini Enterprise and that Gemini models process 22 billion API tokens per minute; these are the company's own adoption figures. The 10-K is equally plain that competitors are rapidly developing and deploying cloud-based services and capacity and that pricing and delivery models are competitive and constantly evolving, so this advantage is being built rather than settled.

moatFactors.name: Distribution through Android, Chrome and Play
moatFactors.body: Android, Chrome, Google Play, Google Maps and Gmail put Google services in front of users and feed the advertising business. The same distribution arrangements are what regulators target: the EC decision in the risks section concerned Google's Android-related distribution agreements. The moat and the main legal risk share a root, so any remedy that reaches distribution would test this factor directly.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat WIDE. Advertising across Search and YouTube, reached through Alphabet's own platforms and through partners paid via TAC, remains the main profit pool, and Google Cloud has become a second one. The threat to durability comes from the technology Alphabet is investing in: the company's 10-K says AI is quickly reshaping the advertising industry, including how ads are delivered online, and that there is no assurance it will adapt effectively and competitively. So far the reported figures show Search revenue growing (growth section), which is why that threat sits in our Bear case rather than our Base. The second pressure is cost. Holding the moat now takes capital spending on a scale the company is partly funding with new equity and debt, so a wide moat does not by itself guarantee wide returns on the new capital. What the valuation underwrites is that Search monetization survives the AI shift; that part of the moat is still being tested.

points: Google Cloud revenue rose {+ 82% +} to $24.8 billion in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, which the company described as a meaningful acceleration, led by Google Cloud Platform across enterprise AI Solutions and enterprise AI Infrastructure as well as core GCP services. Of the quarter's revenue increase, Google Cloud added $11.1 billion and Google Services $12.0 billion, so Cloud now supplies close to half of Alphabet's growth from about a fifth of its revenue.

TPU systems are a new line inside Cloud. Alphabet has signed a limited number of agreements to supply TPU systems to customers who require or provide on-premises infrastructure for specialized, high-scale workloads, began recognizing that revenue in the second quarter of 2026, and expects the significant majority in 2027. The filing gives the timing, not the amount, so this supports FY27 more than FY26 by an unknown margin.

Advertising is still growing. Google Services revenue rose {+ 15% +} to $94.5 billion, with Google Search & other up {+ 17% +} to $63,271 million, Google subscriptions, platforms, and devices up {+ 15% +} and YouTube ads up {+ 13% +}, while Google Network revenue edged down to $7,303 million from $7,354 million. Pichai said AI features are driving Search query growth and the Gemini App has 950 million monthly active users; Search growing faster than Services as a whole is consistent with that claim, though it does not prove it.
Consensus expects revenue of $498.5 billion in FY26E, up {+ 24% +}, and $613.7 billion in FY27E, which is the growth path behind the FY27E earnings our valuation rests on.

Growth at this pace is costing more. Operating expenses grew faster than revenue in the quarter, Other Bets and the central AI research line both lost more than a year earlier, and capital spending absorbed the FY25 rise in operating cash flow. Advertising also stays tied to the economy, which the company names as a driver of advertiser spending.

management.leadership: The proxy filed April 24, 2026 names the five executive officers whose 2025 pay it discusses: Sundar Pichai, Chief Executive Officer of Alphabet and Google and a director; Anat Ashkenazi, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Alphabet and Google; Ruth M. Porat, President and Chief Investment Officer of Alphabet and Google; Philipp Schindler, Senior Vice President and Chief Business Officer of Google; and Kent Walker, President, Global Affairs, Chief Legal Officer and Secretary of Alphabet and Google. Titles are as of that proxy. On the operating line the record is good, with revenue growth and a wider margin in the latest quarter (financials section). Headcount was 198,933 at June 30, 2026 against 187,103 a year earlier, so the company is still adding people while it spends on AI infrastructure. In the July 22, 2026 release Pichai said Alphabet's AI investments are redefining what is possible across every part of its business. The capital program shows management acting on that view; whether it earns an adequate return is the open question the 10-K itself raises.
management.capitalAllocation: The allocation has tilted toward AI infrastructure. In FY25, buybacks fell and dividends rose while capital spending climbed (cash-flow section). In the second quarter of 2026 Alphabet raised new equity and debt and set up an ATM program aimed mainly at employee equity tax obligations (balance-sheet section), so the share count rose between December 31 and June 30 rather than fell. In July 2026 the board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.22 per share on Class A, Class B and Class C stock and $12.15 per share on each series of the mandatory convertible preferred stock. Raising outside capital to build capacity is a reasonable choice for a company in a capital-heavy build-out, but it changes the per-share case. Per-share value now depends on earnings growth outrunning new issuance rather than on buybacks shrinking the count, and the returns on long-lived AI assets are not yet visible in the figures.
management.governance: Governance rests on the DEF 14A proxy filed April 24, 2026. The board applies independence standards that mirror SEC rules and Nasdaq listing rules, and determined that every director nominee is independent except Larry, Sergey and Sundar. The Compensation Committee, whose members during 2025 were L. John Doerr, Ram and Robin, is made up entirely of independent directors and engaged Compensia Inc. and Semler Brossy as consultants that report to it rather than to management. A related-party transaction requires a determination by the Board, acting through the Audit Committee, that it is in the best interests of Alphabet and its shareholders, and any holder of more than five percent of a class of voting securities counts as a related party. Alphabet has three classes of common stock, Class A, Class B and Class C; the captured excerpt does not set out each class's voting rights or who holds the Class B shares, so we do not size voting control. Nothing in the excerpt is a red flag for outside holders. The gap that matters is the one the excerpt leaves open: how votes are distributed across the share classes.
management.insiderOwnership: The captured proxy excerpt does not include the beneficial-ownership table, so no director or officer stake is stated here. It does say the company requires named executive officers and other senior executives to maintain certain levels of holdings of Alphabet shares, and that it uses equity awards that vest over time to align employee and shareholder interests. For outside holders, alignment through pay is documented; the size of insider stakes and their voting weight are not.

idiosyncratic: AI and advertising. In its 10-K filed February 5, 2026, Alphabet says AI is quickly reshaping the advertising industry, including how ads are delivered online, and that there is no assurance it will adapt effectively and competitively. If AI-generated answers reduce the paid clicks the company measures on Google Search & other properties, the core profit pool is exposed. The reported Search growth shows no such effect yet, which is why this risk drives our Bear case rather than our Base.

Regulation of distribution. On July 2, 2026 the EC upheld its 2018 decision that certain provisions in Google's Android-related distribution agreements infringed European antitrust laws; the fine and interest of $5.2 billion had been accrued and was paid in July 2026. That cash cost is behind the company. The larger risk is a remedy that reaches the distribution arrangements the moat section describes. The 10-K also notes that cloud pricing and delivery models are subject to increasing regulatory scrutiny and requirements.

Capacity commitments. The 10-K says Alphabet is entering into significant leasing arrangements with third-party operators to meet AI compute demand and has large, long-duration commercial agreements; in a nonperformance or an industry downturn it may incur additional liabilities, have excess capacity it cannot easily redeploy, and not receive payments. It adds that changes in expected technology advancements could shorten the period over which these assets benefit the business. With capex already absorbing the growth in operating cash flow, a demand slowdown would show up in free cash flow first.

Dilution. The build-out is partly funded with the June 2026 equity raise, mandatory convertible preferred stock and an ATM program (balance-sheet section). If returns on the AI assets arrive late, per-share earnings grow more slowly than the business, and any further equity would widen that gap.

Other Bets. The segment lost more in the quarter than a year earlier (moat section), and the 10-K says these offerings, in areas such as life sciences and transportation, face intense competition from large, experienced, and well-funded competitors and may not be successful or operate at sufficient levels of profitability.
risks.systemic: Advertising spending follows the economy: the 10-K says adverse macroeconomic conditions have affected, and may in the future affect, the demand for advertising. Currency moves reported revenue too, as the gap between reported and constant-currency growth in the quarter shows (financials section). Across the industry, the company notes that competitors are rapidly developing and deploying cloud-based services and capacity; if AI demand slowed while that capacity was still arriving, pricing could weaken for all providers. Regulation spans advertising, data privacy and AI products, which the 10-K says raise ethical, technological, legal, regulatory and other challenges. Reported earnings also now depend on equity markets: the second-quarter gain came primarily from net unrealized gains on equity securities, so a broad fall in the value of those holdings could turn the same line into losses. Against these exposures stand a high operating margin, ample interest coverage and liquid assets well above debt (balance-sheet section), which give Alphabet room to absorb a shock without changing course.

body: We rate Alphabet BUY with a $360–$470 target range. The probability-weighted fair value is $404.18, for expected upside of +15.1% against bear-case downside of 27.8% and a reward/risk of 0.54×. The call rests on the operating line: Cloud and Search are growing, margin is widening, and FY27 consensus earnings, which carry none of the 2026 investment gains, are worth a full multiple a year out if they arrive. It is a narrow BUY. A lower Base multiple, a heavier Bear weight or a slightly higher price each turns it into a HOLD, as the valuation section shows.

We would move to HOLD on a reported quarter in which Google Search & other revenue falls year over year, or on a further equity raise beyond the June 2026 offering and the ATM program. A close above the narrow band around today's price in which these scenarios still derive BUY would also call for a re-run of the scenarios rather than new buying.
